summary.title: Summary
text: Researcher and software developer focused on the intersection of advanced generative AI, structured data synthesis, and privacy-preserving Machine Learning systems.
Investigates the structural limitations of generative architectures in this setting, combining rigorous evaluation of statistical fidelity and memorization risks with practical system development.

items.title: Towards Explainable Governance of Synthetic Health Data in Collaborative Healthcare Ecosystems
items.subtitle: A. Pelusi, A. Trombetta, D. Spoladore, S. Braghin
bullets: Proposed a role-aware Explainable AI framework for the governance of LLM-generated synthetic health data, translating privacy, fidelity, and reliability metrics into stakeholder-specific explanations aligned with GDPR and the EU AI Act.

items.title: Privacy-Fidelity Trade-offs in Differentially Private Synthetic Tabular Data Generation
items.subtitle: A. Pelusi, S. Braghin, A. Trombetta
bullets: Evaluated differentially private LoRA fine-tuning (DP-SGD via Opacus) for LLM-based tabular synthesis, characterizing the privacy-fidelity frontier and the feature-level degradation on high-cardinality categorical attributes.

items.title: Categorical Prior Lock-in: Why In-Context Learning Fails for Structured Data
items.subtitle: A. Pelusi, S. Braghin, A. Trombetta
bullets: Compared in-context learning and LoRA fine-tuning for LLM-based tabular synthesis, identifying categorical prior lock-in, the failure of ICL to reproduce high-cardinality categorical distributions, and its trade-off with memorization risk.

items.title: synth-pipeline
items.subtitle: Privacy-Preserving Synthetic Tabular Data Generation Pipeline
bullets: Architected an end-to-end pipeline for privacy-preserving tabular data synthesis: LLMs are fine-tuned with LoRA to generate schema-validated records, with optional Differential Privacy training via Opacus at a configurable epsilon.

Devised a rigorous evaluation framework assessing statistical fidelity (TVD, correlation error), downstream utility (TSTR) and privacy risk (distance to closest record, k-anonymity, membership inference attacks).
